title: The Order Database
briefing: The website is taking orders, but they're vanishing every time the server restarts! Orders need to live in a database. We're using MongoDB, which stores each order as a document that looks just like a Python dict. Add new orders, find the pending ones, ship some, and cancel one.
hints: client = MongoClient("mongodb://localhost:27017"), then db = client["byteworks"] and orders = db["orders"]. insert_one takes a dict and insert_many takes a list of dicts.

find({"status": "pending"}) returns the matching documents (wrap it in list()). count_documents works the same way. Updates need $set: update_one({"order_id": 3}, {"$set": {"status": "shipped"}}). Operators like {"$gte": 1000} compare values.

orders.insert_one(new_order) / orders.insert_many(more_orders) / pending = list(orders.find({"status": "pending"})) / big_spenders = list(orders.find({"price": {"$gte": 1000}})) / orders.update_one({"order_id": ship_id}, {"$set": {"status": "shipped"}}) / orders.delete_one({"order_id": cancel_id}) / pending_count = orders.count_documents({"status": "pending"})
bonus: Use update_many with {"$inc": {"price": 10}} to add a £10 delivery charge to every pending order.
